title: Complementary components of a reduced pure subcurve
statement: Let $X$ be a reduced Noetherian scheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], where Noetherian means locally Noetherian and quasi-compact (every open cover has a finite subcover). Suppose every irreducible component of $X$ [def-weil-irreducible-components] has topological Krull dimension $1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $Y\subseteq X$ be a reduced closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion] all of whose irreducible components have dimension $1$. Let $Z\subseteq X$ be the reduced induced closed subscheme on $\overline{|X|\setminus|Y|}$ [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. There is a subset $I$ of the finite set of irreducible components of $X$ such that $Y$ is the reduced closed union of the components in $I$ and $Z$ is the reduced closed union of all remaining components. Every irreducible component of $Z$ has dimension $1$, and the reduced induced closed subscheme on $\overline{|X|\setminus|Z|}$ is $Y$. Empty $Y$ and empty $Z$ are allowed; the component dimension condition for the empty scheme is vacuous.

source.place: Tag 0E38 (lemma-closed-subscheme-nodal-curve), first paragraph of the proof: reduced equidimensional one-dimensional closed subschemes are unions of components; the complementary-union and double-complement consequences require no nodal hypothesis.

proof.text: The components of the Noetherian scheme $X$ form a finite set by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components]. Component coverage [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover] applies to $X$ and $Y$. The proof works uniformly when either scheme or either component union is empty.

source.place: Tag 0E38 first paragraph, with the Noetherian component-finiteness input

proof.text: For a component $C$ of $Y$, its image under the closed embedding $i$ is closed and irreducible. By [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover] it lies in an ambient component $D$. Restricting $i$ gives a closed embedding $C\to D$. If it were not surjective, its range would have nonempty open complement $U$ in the irreducible space $D$. By [new-node-irreducible-open-complement-dimension], the closed complement of $U$ is empty or has dimension at most an integer $e<1$, hence at most zero. The embedding identifies $C$ homeomorphically with this complement, contradicting its dimension one. Therefore the image of $C$ equals $D$.

source.place: Tag 0E38 first paragraph: a reduced equidimensional one-dimensional closed subscheme is a union of irreducible components

proof.text: Define $I$ as the set of images under $i$ of the components of $Y$. Step 2 shows $I\subseteq\operatorname{Irr}(X)$. Component coverage [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover] shows $\operatorname{range}(i)=\bigcup I$, since every point of $Y$ lies on a component and every component image is contained in the range.

source.place: Tag 0E38 first paragraph and the reduced-induced uniqueness statement

proof.text: For any subset $S$ of the finite ambient component set, prove $\overline{(\bigcup S)^c}=\bigcup(\operatorname{Irr}(X)\setminus S)$. The right side is closed, and component coverage [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover] puts every point outside the selected union in it. Conversely, for a component $D$ outside $S$, Mathlib closure_sUnion_irreducibleComponents_sdiff_singleton identifies $D$ with the closure of the complement of the union of all other components. Since $S$ is contained among those other components, closure monotonicity puts $D$ in the desired closure. Apply this identity to $I$ and use the stipulated range of $j$.

source.place: Tag 0E38 (lemma-closed-subscheme-nodal-curve), first paragraph, with the finite-component closure argument written out; Tags 004W (lemma-irreducible) and 01IS (lemma-scheme-sober).

proof.text: For a component $C$ of $Z$, its irreducible image is contained in the finite closed cover by components $D$ outside $I$. Mathlib isIrreducible_iff_sUnion_isClosed puts that image in one such $D$. Since all of $D$ lies in the range of the embedding $j$, its preimage is homeomorphic to $D$ and is irreducible. It contains $C$, so maximality of $C$ makes the preimage equal to $C$. Thus $j(C)=D$, and the homeomorphism preserves dimension. Apply the hypothesis on the dimensions of ambient components. If $Z$ is empty there are no components to check.

source.place: Tag 0E38 (lemma-closed-subscheme-nodal-curve), first paragraph, with the finite-component closure argument written out; Tags 004W (lemma-irreducible) and 01IS (lemma-scheme-sober).

proof.text: Apply the component-union closure identity of Step 4 again to $\operatorname{Irr}(X)\setminus I$. Set difference cancellation gives $\overline{\operatorname{range}(j)^c}=\bigcup I=\operatorname{range}(i)$. The uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme], applied to the given reduced closed immersion $i$, provides the required isomorphism to the vanishing-ideal subscheme and its equality over $X$. The same argument includes empty and full component selections.

source.place: Tag 0E38 (lemma-closed-subscheme-nodal-curve), first paragraph, with the finite-component closure argument written out; Tags 004W (lemma-irreducible) and 01IS (lemma-scheme-sober).

lean.statement: theorem complementary_pure_subcurve_components {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} [IsReduced X] [IsNoetherian X] (hX : ∀ C ∈ irreducibleComponents X, topologicalKrullDim C = 1) (i : Y ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsReduced Y] (hY : ∀ C ∈ irreducibleComponents Y, topologicalKrullDim C = 1) (j : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion j] [IsReduced Z] (hZ : Set.range j = closure ((Set.range i)ᶜ)) : ∃ I : Set (Set X), I ⊆ irreducibleComponents X ∧ Set.range i = ⋃₀ I ∧ Set.range j = ⋃₀ (irreducibleComponents X \ I) ∧ (∀ C ∈ irreducibleComponents Z, topologicalKrullDim C = 1) ∧ ∃ e : Y ≅ (Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal (Closeds.closure ((Set.range j)ᶜ))).subscheme, e.hom ≫ (Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal (Closeds.closure ((Set.range j)ᶜ))).subschemeι = i
